evals.prompt: Refine GitHub issue #42 in acme/widgets — it was synced from the roadmap and just has a source checklist, I need real acceptance criteria before I assign it.
expected_behavior: Fetches issue #42 and reads its current body (Roadmap ID, Category, Score, source checklist)
Rewrites the description as a short user-facing summary with no code references
Writes acceptance criteria as observable behavior, each tagged [unit]/[integration]/[e2e]
Runs the script in --dry-run and confirms VALIDATION: PASS before asking to apply
Applies only after explicit user confirmation, editing the live issue via gh issue edit

evals.prompt: This issue is too vague to build: 'make the signup form better'. Turn it into a proper spec with testable acceptance criteria and a clear description.
expected_behavior: Treats the plain issue (no source checklist) as valid input and still produces ACs
Writes behavioral ACs (e.g. inline errors on empty fields, no record created) rather than implementation steps
Classifies each AC by test type so the implementer knows which test proves it
Self-checks that no file/module/function names leak into the AC before dry-run

evals.prompt: Add acceptance criteria to issue #42 and tighten the title. Don't push anything to GitHub until I've looked at the proposed body.
expected_behavior: Defaults to --dry-run and prints the proposed title + refined body + validation result
Does NOT run --apply (no live edit) without explicit confirmation
Shows the before -> after so the user can review before consenting
On later --apply, refuses (non-zero) if the AC validation fails
